## Human review verdict — chalbert/web-everything#1526

**Verdict:** ✅ pass — no blocking findings

### Panel verdicts

| lens | weight | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| correctness | mandatory | accept |

### Findings (1)

**correctness** (1)
- `scripts/lib/skill-operation-wiring.mjs:274` — extractOperationCalls captures a match's argv tail greedily up to the next backtick/newline, so when two `run.mjs <op> ...` invocations sit on the same physical line with no backtick between them (e.g. inside a fenced fenced code block, chained with `&&`), the second invocation is swallowed whole into the first's flag list instead of being scanned as its own call. — A doc/skill line reading `node scripts/operations/run.mjs scaffold --title=x && node scripts/operations/run.mjs resolve --ref=5` (a natural way to show a two-step workflow inside a fenced code block, and the same fenced-block convention the PR's own round-1 fix was written around) is parsed as ONE call to `scaffold` with flags `['title', 'ref']`. Verified directly: `extractOperationCalls` returns a single entry `{op: 'scaffold', flags: ['title','ref']}` and `findMalformedOperationCalls` then emits a false ERROR — 'operation call passes a flag `scaffold` does not declare: --ref' — against a perfectly well-formed pair of calls, while `resolve`'s own invocation (and any real defect in it, e.g. a genuinely unknown flag) is never independently judged at all. If the second call's flag name happens to coincide with a field the first operation *does* declare, the failure flips silently the other way: the second call's real defect goes completely unreported. No test in skill-operation-wiring.test.mjs exercises two invocations on one physical line — I grepped the test file for '&&' / 'run.mjs.*run.mjs' and found nothing, and grepped skills-src/docs for the same shape and found nothing currently in the tree, so this is dormant today but not covered by any of the 46 wiring tests. _[impact if unfixed: degraded]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ A regression test pinning 'two run.mjs invocations chained on one line are scanned as two independent calls' (mirroring the six existing defect-class tests already in this file) would catch this whole class; the durable fix is bounding OPERATION_CALL's tail capture with a lookahead that stops before the next `node .../run.mjs` rather than running to the next backtick/newline.

---

**Decision:** `accept` — recorded by operator.
**Lens:** `correctness` — a SINGLE-LENS run. One `judge` step, one juror, one lens; the table above lists only the lens that judged. The other 3 panel lenses (security, simplicity, standards-conformance) did NOT run and are not reported as unjudged.
Net basis: `f01b2285b443de3e09d75a38d9ee7e2837d051a0..a9e26d5eeca4fa0183e340593e134901a9b16ae9` (rev `origin/lane/3253-argv-equivalence` at review time) — 7 net changed file(s) vs current main (#2450), not `gh pr diff`'s three-dot list.

_Recorded through the declared `review-pr` operation (#3035)._
